title: Conformance fixture, v1
description: A language-neutral test case: a workflow, a sequence of turns, and the expected normalized results. Every runtime binding reads these files; no runtime ships its own copy.

requires.description: capability ids the runtime must declare as supported to run this fixture. A runtime that declares any of them unsupported skips the fixture and records skipped, never a pass.

workflow_ref.description: path to a workflow document, relative to the fixture file

signal.description: resumes a suspended turn instead of starting a new one

advance_time_ms.description: advance the runtime's logical clock before this turn; runtimes without logical time declare timers unsupported

restart_runtime.description: restart or recover the runtime before this turn, exercising replay and recovery

user_id.description: the user the turn or signal claims; default anonymous. Beside a principal it means nothing

principal.description: who the turn or signal is authenticated as, as a gateway or an embedding program vouches for it

crash_at.description: kill this delivery at a named point, then recover the runtime from whatever it keeps across a crash. The delivery's result has status crashed.

event.description: crash around the append of this event type

call.description: crash around the execution of this tool

when.description: event: before or after the append. call: before the tool runs; during, once it has run and before its outcome is journaled; after, once the outcome is journaled and before it is logged

concurrent_with.description: turn ids delivered concurrently with this one; the runtime must still apply them in the declared order

status_any.description: the status is one of these. Only for a point where a log that rolled back and a log that did not may honestly differ, such as a crash after the terminal event

events.description: the exact sequence of event types of this result: nothing extra, nothing missing

event_payloads.description: each entry names the first event of `type` in the result, or its `occurrence`, and a subset of its payload

event_fields.description: fields every event of the result must carry

reply_matches.description: ECMA-262 regular expression, matched with search semantics

tool_calls.description: exact sequence of tool calls, compared on tool id, index, args, and attempt

events_include.description: event types that must appear, in this relative order
